_README: Provenance-free restatements of claims, used ONLY to build the referee's
submission. The ledger statement reaches the referee verbatim, and ours
narrate project history -- 'CORRECTION of C0009', 'the Phase 0 audit set
this as island 01's opening target', 'discharges (Z1) of byrnes_audit.md'.
That tells an adversarial reader what answer is wanted and cites documents
it cannot see, which defeats the gate.
A restatement must say the SAME mathematics as the claim, with the project
narrative removed and nothing added. It must not weaken or hedge the claim:
the referee should be able to reject the restatement exactly when it would
reject the original. These are committed so the substitution is auditable;
referee.py records in each verdict that a restatement was used, and which.
Claims absent from this file are refereed on their ledger statement, with
any leak recorded in the verdict as a noted bias.
C0012: For all integers q >= r >= 0, f(q,r) <= q + r + 1. Consequently, for each fixed r the quantity f(q,r) - q is at most r + 1 for every q >= r.
C0021: For every P-position (p,q,r) of 3-row Chomp with r >= 1, p - q <= 3r - 1. Equivalently, for each fixed r, f(q,r) - q is at most 3r - 1 for every q >= r.
C0024: Let f(q,r) be the unique p such that (p,q,r) is a P-position of 3-row Chomp, defined by the Brouwer recurrence; for each fixed r let N(r) be the least q0 >= r such that the sequence f(q,r)-q is periodic for all q >= q0 (if row r has only finitely many P-positions, i.e. f(q,r) < q for all large q, N(r) is instead the least q with f(q,r) < q). Define B_c(a)=f(c+a,c)-(c+a) (undefined where no loser [c,a,b] exists), u_c=N(c)-c, p_c=the period of f(q,c)-q for q >= N(c) (p_c:=1 for rows with finitely many P-positions), q_r=lcm{p_c : 0<=c<r}, m_r=1+max{B_c(a) : 0<=c<r, a>=0}, U_r=max{u_c:c<r}, t_r=max(U_r,r). Then for every r>=1: (i) m_r<=r+1; (ii) p_r<=q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r); (iii) u_r<=max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r); (iv) q_{r+1}<=q_r^2(r+2)^(r+1). Hence N(r)<=r+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r) for rows with infinitely many P-positions, and N(r)<=r+1+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r) otherwise. Every quantity on the right is computed from the rows c<r alone, so this is an effective recursion for N(r).
C0027: Let f(q,r) be the unique p such that (p,q,r) is a P-position of 3-row Chomp, defined by the Brouwer recurrence; for each fixed r let N(r) be the least q0 such that f(q,r)-q is eventually periodic in q for all q >= q0. Define a priori sequences g,h by g(1)=1, g(r+1)=g(r)^2 (r+2)^(r+1), and h(r)=11+r+sum_{k=2}^{r} g(k)(k+2)^(k+1). Then for every r>=1, N(r) <= r + h(r). The bound is explicit and computable (g(r)=2^{Theta(2^r)}, so N(r) <= 2^{2^{O(r)}}), and no quantity on the right is defined by a recursion over the actual rows.
C0028: Let f(q,r) be the unique p such that (p,q,r) is a P-position of 3-row Chomp, defined by the Brouwer recurrence; for each fixed r let N(r) be the least q0 >= r such that the sequence f(q,r)-q is periodic for all q >= q0 (if row r has only finitely many P-positions, i.e. f(q,r) < q for all large q, N(r) is instead the least q with f(q,r) < q). Define a priori sequences g,h by g(1)=1, g(r+1)=g(r)(r+2)^(r+1), and h(r)=11+r+sum_{k=2}^{r} g(k)(k+2)^(k+1). Then for every r>=1, N(r) <= r+h(r), with g(r)=prod_{k=1}^{r-1}(k+2)^{k+1}, so N(r) <= 2^{O(r^2 log r)}. The bound is explicit and computable and no quantity on the right is defined by a recursion over the actual rows.
